scenes.headline: Why Money and Hours Leak Between Paychecks
bullets: Federal Reserve survey: 37% would borrow, sell, or come up short
Peter Drucker (1967): memory always lies about where time goes
scenes.narration: According to the Federal Reserve's Survey of Household Economics and Decisionmaking, thirty-seven percent of American adults could not cover an unexpected four-hundred-dollar expense using cash or its equivalent alone. In 1967, management writer Peter Drucker noticed the exact same blind spot with time: when executives guessed how they spent their week, their memory was wrong every single time. Most people lose both money and focus in tiny unrecorded leaks. You can fix both in thirty minutes every Sunday afternoon.
scenes.source: Federal Reserve SHED Report (Fig. 21); Peter Drucker, The Effective Executive (1967)

scenes.headline: Why Spreadsheets Quit and Bank Bots Risk Data
scenes.left_body: Typing every $4 receipt by hand or giving apps bank logins
scenes.right_body: Strip name + account digits locally, then classify in 60 seconds
scenes.narration: Traditional budgeting fails for a simple reason: logging every four-dollar coffee by hand drains willpower, so most people quit inside three weeks. Yet the modern shortcut of handing live bank usernames and passwords to unverified third-party apps creates an unnecessary security exposure. A safer alternative uses the plain CSV statement your bank already lets you download, with zero live account connection.

scenes.headline: The 3-Bucket AI Statement Sort
scenes.stat_label: FIXED BILLS • GENUINE VALUE • FORGOTTEN LEAKS
bullets: Delete name and account columns from your CSV in 30 seconds
Ask AI to flag duplicate renewals, fee hikes, and unused trials
scenes.narration: Spend the first ten minutes on cash clarity. Open your recent card CSV, delete the column with your name or card digits, and paste only dates, merchant names, and dollar amounts into your AI workspace. Ask it to group every line into three buckets: essential fixed bills, purchases you genuinely valued, and forgotten recurring charges or price creeps. Cancel one unused renewal on the spot.

scenes.headline: Paul Graham's Maker vs Manager Calendar Audit
bullets: One mid-afternoon meeting splits 4 open hours into shallow halves
Lock two uninterrupted 90-minute focus blocks before Monday starts
scenes.narration: Spend minutes ten through twenty on your calendar. In his 2009 essay Maker's Schedule, Manager's Schedule, programmer Paul Graham explained how a single thirty-minute meeting in the middle of an afternoon breaks four open hours into two fragments too short for serious creation. Look at the coming week right now, cluster routine errands onto one afternoon, and lock two uninterrupted ninety-minute blocks for skill or asset building.

scenes.headline: Automate Payday Routing Before Willpower Fades
bullets: Schedule automatic transfers for the day after payday
Spend whatever remains guilt-free without daily tracking
scenes.narration: Use the final ten minutes to verify your upcoming automatic transfers. Author Ramit Sethi popularized a straightforward rule in I Will Teach You To Be Rich: decide your savings and investment percentages once, schedule those transfers for the day right after your paycheck lands, and spend the remaining checking balance without guilt. When money moves automatically on day one, impulse moods on Friday night cannot touch your future margin.
scenes.source: Federal Reserve SHED Table 16; Ramit Sethi, I Will Teach You To Be Rich (2019)

scenes.headline: Twenty-Six Calm Hours Reshape an Entire Year
scenes.stat_label: 52 SUNDAYS X 30 MINUTES = 26 HOURS PER YEAR
scenes.narration: Thirty minutes every Sunday adds up to just twenty-six hours across an entire year. Yet those fifty-two small checkpoints catch silent fee increases early and guard over one hundred and fifty hours of focused creative work.
